in_latin.name: Elliottus
in_latin.meaning: English origin, variant of Elliott with Anglo-Saxon roots
in_latin.long_meaning: Derived from Old English 'Eadgriyth' and 'Eadric', meaning noble and ruler, respectively, Elliot is a variant of Elliott, which is associated with the Anglo-Saxon tribe 'Ealdorman', a high-ranking official. In Christian tradition, the name signifies nobility, power, and leadership, reflecting the values of the early Christian church.
